questions.q: What are the four parts of every HTTP request?
questions.explain: A request is made of a method (GET/POST/etc.), a URL, headers, and an optional body.

questions.q: Where do query parameters like ?spacecraft=Apollo11 live?
options: In the URL itself, appended after a "?"
In a separate file sent alongside the request
They don't exist in HTTP — only in Postman
questions.explain: Query parameters are key/value pairs appended to the URL after a "?", as shown in the real Postman request screenshot.

questions.q: What are the three parts of every HTTP response?
questions.explain: A response opens with a status line (e.g. HTTP/1.1 200 OK), followed by headers, then an optional body.

questions.q: In the real response screenshot showing "200 OK · 100 ms · 1.03 KB", which part of the response does "200 OK" represent?
questions.explain: "200 OK" is the status line — the very first thing a response communicates, before headers or body.

questions.q: Which HTTP methods conventionally carry a request body, and which conventionally don't?
options: POST, PUT, and PATCH commonly carry a body; GET conventionally does not
All methods always carry a body
No method ever carries a body
questions.explain: POST, PUT, and PATCH typically send data in the body; GET requests rely on the URL (path and query parameters) and conventionally omit a body.
